item.description: The University of Papua New Guinea council in its meeting today, announced the appointment of an independent investigation panel to look into the allegations of “unacceptable conduct” in its administration. This after Professor Ian Findlay voluntarily resigned last week alleging ongoing unacceptable conduct by Chancellor Sir Robert Igara, who was in turn asked to step down by Prime Minister James
item.content:encoded:
The University of Papua New Guinea council in its meeting today, announced the appointment of an independent investigation panel to look into the allegations of “unacceptable conduct” in its administration.

This after Professor Ian Findlay voluntarily resigned last week alleging ongoing unacceptable conduct by Chancellor Sir Robert Igara, who was in turn asked to step down by Prime Minister James Marape.

Students held a sit in protest yesterday (Tuesday 03.11.26) calling for the immediate reinstatement of Findlay and resignation of Sir Robert.

The council also formally announced the appointment of Acting Chancellor Goiye Gileng and Acting Vice Chancellor Professor Betty Lovai.

In a media statement this afternoon, Mr. Gileng says the special council meeting also formally received the complaints and allegations of the former VC and accepted the “voluntary leave of absence” by Igara pending the outcome of the independent investigation.

Gileng has assured students, parents and stakeholders that the council is in control and its business as usual.

The Acting Chancellor is expected to immediately submit a report of the actions taken to the Minister of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology.

item.title: Three new land commissioners sworn into office
item.description: The Papua New Guinea Land Commission has appointed three new commissioners to help resolve land disputes and oversee special projects in mining areas. The three commissioners were sworn into office by Governor-General Sir Bob Dadae at Government House on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
The Papua New Guinea Land Commission has appointed three new commissioners to help resolve land disputes and oversee special projects in mining areas.

The three commissioners were sworn into office by Governor-General Sir Bob Dadae at Government House on Tuesday.

The Land Commission was established under the Land Act 2022, bringing together the functions of the Lands Titles Commission, which deals with customary land matters, and the National Lands Commission, which handles land acquired during the colonial period.

In a small but significant ceremony witnessed by family members, Immanuel Sawan was appointed Commissioner of Lands for a four-year term.

He will initially handle land matters in the National Capital District and Central Province before extending his work to other provinces.

Former magistrates Mark Selifkaro and Cosmas Bidar have been appointed for six months to oversee special projects in the Gobe and Kainantu mining areas.

Chief Lands Commissioner Molean Kilepak welcomed the appointments, saying the commissioners' knowledge and experience would help address land disputes and other challenges across the country.

Under the law, commissioners must be sworn into office before they can carry out their judicial duties.

Mr Sawan said his immediate priority would be to address pending cases.

“I think the immediate priority is to work on hearings for NCD centres and other pending matters, depending on the funding that we are able to share and the Chief Commissioner's directions,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Land Commission plans to establish regional offices in Milne Bay, Vanimo, Manus and Imbonggu.

item.title: Police officer identified in Rainbow drive by shooting
item.description: Police have confirmed a drive-by shooting outside Eliseo Rainbow Shopping Centre in Port Moresby this afternoon, identifying the alleged shooter as a police officer. Assistant Commissioner of Police for NCD and Central Command, Benjamin Turi, confirmed the incident to NBC News but did not provide further details.
item.content:encoded:
Police have confirmed a drive-by shooting outside Eliseo Rainbow Shopping Centre in Port Moresby this afternoon, identifying the alleged shooter as a police officer.

Assistant Commissioner of Police for NCD and Central Command, Benjamin Turi, confirmed the incident to NBC News but did not provide further details.

CCTV footage circulating on social media appears to show a grey, five-door Toyota Land Cruiser pulling out of the shopping centre before a man allegedly opened fire on another man standing near the Rainbow Big Rooster bus stop.

The man was among two others when the shooting occurred.

In a separate video circulating online, the victim, who is from the Highlands region, recounted what he said happened.

He claimed the occupants of the unmarked vehicle called out to him as they drove out of the shopping centre. He said he responded that he was heading to Four Mile before turning away to continue walking towards the bus stop.

He alleged that he was grazed by a bullet, after which the shooter approached him and searched his belongings. The shooter then returned to the vehicle and fled the scene, according to the victim.

Social media speculation has linked the shooting to killings reported over the weekend. However, police have urged the public not to spread unverified information.

In a statement on its official page, the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary confirmed that the alleged shooter had been identified as a police officer and would be dealt with accordingly.

ACP Turi urged the public to refrain from spreading misinformation that could create fear among city residents.

Police investigations are also continuing into other recent incidents.

item.content:encoded:

item.title: Gelmon Clan gets title after 6 years as ENB moves to stop fake ILGs and land grab
item.description: A customary land group in East New Britain has been issued its ILG certificate after six years of work. The Gilmo Clan of Sulka in the Bitapaka LLG in Kokopo District acquired its certificate on Thursday last week, becoming one of several groups to receive theirs in recent years under new strict ILG laws.
item.content:encoded:
A customary land group in East New Britain has been issued its ILG certificate after six years of work.

The Gilmo Clan of Sulka in the Bitapaka LLG in Kokopo District acquired its certificate on Thursday last week, becoming one of several groups to receive theirs in recent years under new strict ILG laws.

Members of the Gelmon clan and nearby villages gathered at the Ganai village ceremonial ground, a few kilometres outside Kokopo Town, to celebrate the occasion

The certificate was presented by ILG Registrar Augustine Kapanombo who travelled from Port Moresby to hand deliver it to the clan leaders.

For the Gelmon Clan, it is not just a paper. It is legal recognition that they are the customary owners of their land.

“ The purpose of it is to free up your customary land, the title remains under you, for your own security and your own development aspirations, for the province and for the country as a whole”, Mr. Kapanombo said.

It took the clan six years to put together the requirements.

Under the new ILG law, a clan must provide their family history, a map of their customary land boundaries and forms of identifications of all its members among others.

The Gelmon ILG’s secretary, George Barob explained, “The education level of many clan members is a big problem. They can understand some of the talks about registering land, but not everything, so it takes a long time. You have to explain three or four times before they understand and we work together”.

The East New Britain Provincial Government supports the idea. But it is cautious too.

Governor Michael Marum who was part of the occasion told the landowners that they did the right thing. But they have to be careful.

"If we do not look after our land, we will lose it to foreigners. People from other countries will come and grab it from us, and we will sit on our own land and just watch them. And we do not want that”, Marum said.

The group is among several to receive its certificate in recent years, after the ILG concept was flagged for misconception and to a larger extent misused.

Fake ILGs, controlled by just two or three members were used to obtain Special Agriculture Business Leases or SABLs, leasing customary land for up to 99 years to large foreign companies.

Such as in Pomio District where 11 SABLs covering 350,000 hectares were issued using fake indigenous groups which prompted the national government to revise the ILG law and make it rigorous.

A Gelmon clan member, Tom Meriba said “We are now seeing the benefits of what we are working towards. In the future, our next generation will not have to sweat over these issues. They will come and enjoy the things we are fighting and talking about today”.

With the certificate, Gelmon Clan leaders said they will now be able to survey their land, apply for a customary land title and engage with developers, stressing that their land is not for sale but for protection.

They said they are ready for any development that may require their customary land as Kokopo slowly transforms, from a town into a city.

item.title: 25 public servants resign to contest 2027 national elections
item.description: A female is among the 25 public servants that have formally resigned from their positions to contest the 2027 National Elections. The resignations follow the closure of the statutory deadline on October 29, in accordance with Section 55 of the Public Service Management Act 1995.
item.content:encoded:
A female is among the 25 public servants that have formally resigned from their positions to contest the 2027 National Elections.

The resignations follow the closure of the statutory deadline on October 29, in accordance with Section 55 of the Public Service Management Act 1995.

Statistics released by the Department of Personnel Management shows that the 25 resignations came from various regions across the country.

The National Capital District recorded the highest number, with 13 public servants resigning, followed by the Highlands Region with seven, Momase two, the New Guinea Islands with two, and the Southern Region with one.

In a statement, DPM Secretary Taies Sansan clarified that public servants who resign to contest an election formally cease their employment in the public service.

She said the substantive positions previously occupied by those officers would therefore become vacant.

Sansan emphasized that the closure of the resignation deadline marked an important step in ensuring public servants comply with the legal requirements governing their participation in next year's election.

However, Sansan did not clarify whether those who resign to contest the elections but are unsuccessful would be eligible for reappointment to the public service.

item.title: ToBaining urges Kokopo landowners to register customary land as town plans expansion
item.description: Kokopo MP Ereman ToBaining Junior has urged landowners in Kokopo District to register their customary land and obtain legitimate titles. He made the call during the handing over of the ILG certificate to the Gelmon Clan in the Bitapaka LLG on Thursday last week.
item.content:encoded:
Kokopo MP Ereman ToBaining Junior has urged landowners in Kokopo District to register their customary land and obtain legitimate titles.

He made the call during the handing over of the ILG certificate to the Gelmon Clan in the Bitapaka LLG on Thursday last week.

ToBaining Junior said Kokopo will become a city and for that to happen, it needs to partner with traditional landowners to expand its city boundary.

“There is a government process and system that must be followed and no one should attempt to bypass it”, the Kokopo MP said.

The township has grown in the last three decades since the relocation of the provincial capital from Rabaul following the 1994 volcanic eruption.

Since the relocation, Kokopo has seen exponential growth. However, rapid urbanization has brought challenges.

The Kokopo City Authority that has been in charge of the town’s expansion knows all too well, if the city is to grow, there has to be land made available to cater for it.

Mr ToBaining Jnr., was part of an event on Thursday where the Gelmon Clan of Bitapaka Local Level Government received their ILG certificate, giving them rightful ownership to their customary land.

He used the occasion to remind the people that the Kokopo City Authority plans to expand its boundaries and partner with traditional landowners to transform Kokopo from a town into a city.

A City Boundary Committee has since been setup to carry out awareness and gauge views from traditional landowners living along the fringes of the town, such as the Gelmon clan and how they can actively participate in the town’s expansion.

The Kokopo MP says all untitled land must be titled so that when the government moves in with development, the very people to benefit will be the rightful landowners.

“Kokopo City Authority is trying to put you in a space of registering yourself to become a partner in the development of the city and the development of the province,” Mr ToBaining said.

In the coming years, the growth of the town would have doubled.

Issues of overcrowding, strain on public utilities and unplanned land use have sparked concerns among the town planners and even the landowners.

Expanding the city boundary would mean negotiating with the traditional landowners, who for the most part they may not be willing to give up their land.

item.title: UPNG Chancellor to respond to Vice-Chancellor’s resignation
item.description: UPNG Chancellor Sir Robert Igara has told NBC News he will issue an official statement on Tuesday, following a council meeting. It follows the resignation of Vice-Chancellor Professor Ian Findlay.
item.content:encoded:
UPNG Chancellor Sir Robert Igara has told NBC News he will issue an official statement on Tuesday, following a council meeting.

It follows the resignation of Vice-Chancellor Professor Ian Findlay.

Professor Findlay resigned with immediate effect today, Monday, November 2, after 15 months in the position.

In his resignation letter, he said ongoing disagreements with the Chancellor over the governance and management of the university had made it difficult for him to continue.

He also accused the Chancellor of alleged bullying and disrespect, referring to their confrontation at a special council meeting on October 28.

Professor Findlay said he had made progress in improving the university's finances, academic standards, administration and student services during his time in office.

However, he raised concerns over a recent student riot and claims threats to his personal safety had forced him to leave the country.

He said he remained proud of the reforms achieved and hoped.
